scope.description: Consequence probe: what the rest of the cluster loses when a majority of nodes' actors are parked by unconsumed event streams.
assumptions: 3 nodes, majority quorum 2; only node 1 consumes its event stream
same in-process transport and error-free memory storage as the other cases
event_capacity 8 on all nodes so the bound is reached quickly
excluded: any claim that a deployment reaches the bound in a given time

basis.prefix: Three real OmniPaxos instances (pid 1,2,3) over MemoryStorage, each driven by a real omnipaxos_runtime actor from spawn_actor with a harness-local tokio-backed AsyncRuntime impl; one in-process transport task per node forwards outgoing messages to the receiver's handle_incoming. RuntimeConfig: tick_period 2ms, egress_period 1ms, append_notify_timeout 1500ms; case 1/2 use event_capacity 64, case 3 uses 8. ServerConfig: election_tick_timeout 3, resend_message_tick_timeout 5, batch_size 1. Case 3 subscribes and drains events only on pid 1; pids 2 and 3 leave the receiver the handle owns unread, so after enough observed transitions their event channels fill and their actors park. It keeps paced ordinary writes coming from the elected leader, waits until two of the three nodes stop answering commands, then requires: node 1 still answers; node 1's `append_notify_with_timeout(_, 300ms)` resolves with Timeout (its own actor runs, so that endpoint is reachable) rather than Ok; node 1's decided index is unchanged one second later. It emits CA_EVENT parked_majority_cluster {nodes_parked,healthy_node_responsive,append_notify_timeout_reached,decided_before,decided_after}.

before.description: Bounded probe of whether an event stream the application does not consume (bounded by RuntimeConfig::event_capacity) parks the single actor loop and withholds its command/append_notify endpoints, with a drained-stream control in the same execution.
assumptions: 3 nodes, majority quorum, no message loss or reordering beyond the in-process transport, one tokio runtime in one process
event_capacity 64 so the bound is reached inside a bounded window; the source-settled mechanism (send awaits when the channel holds event_capacity events) is capacity-independent
the handle's event receiver exists from construction, so an application that never subscribes still leaves it unread
excluded: schedule independence or any rate bound

after.description: Consequence probe: what the rest of the cluster loses when a majority of nodes' actors are parked by unconsumed event streams.
assumptions: 3 nodes, majority quorum 2; only node 1 consumes its event stream
same in-process transport and error-free memory storage as the other cases
event_capacity 8 on all nodes so the bound is reached quickly
excluded: any claim that a deployment reaches the bound in a given time

prefix.before: Three real OmniPaxos instances (pid 1,2,3) built with OmniPaxosConfig::build over omnipaxos_storage::memory_storage::MemoryStorage, each driven by a real omnipaxos_runtime actor from spawn_actor with a harness-local tokio-backed AsyncRuntime impl; one in-process transport task per node forwards each message from that node's outgoing_messages() to msg.get_receiver()'s handle_incoming. RuntimeConfig: tick_period 2ms, egress_period 1ms, event_capacity 64, append_notify_timeout 1500ms; ServerConfig: election_tick_timeout 3, resend_message_tick_timeout 5, batch_size 1, flush_batch_tick_timeout 100. Ordinary appends are paced at 4ms so consecutive decided-index changes are observed in separate ticks; a burst would decide many entries inside one tick gap and emit a single amalgamated event. Case unconsumed_event_stream_stops_actor_loop leaves each node's event receiver unread (the handle owns one from spawn_actor even if the application never calls subscribe_events) and emits CA_EVENT unconsumed_event_bound_reached {nodes_full,nodes,event_capacity}, CA_EVENT actor_parked {node,samples_without_reply,reply_budget_ms,permanently_parked} and CA_EVENT append_notify_endpoint_withheld {node,per_call_deadline_ms,actor_timeout_ms,outer_wait_ms,resolved}. Case drained_event_stream_keeps_actor_loop_running is the control with one difference, a task per node draining the same stream, and emits CA_EVENT control_actors_responsive {nodes_answering,nodes,event_capacity} and CA_EVENT control_append_notify {origin,succeeded,idx}.
prefix.after: Three real OmniPaxos instances (pid 1,2,3) over MemoryStorage, each driven by a real omnipaxos_runtime actor from spawn_actor with a harness-local tokio-backed AsyncRuntime impl; one in-process transport task per node forwards outgoing messages to the receiver's handle_incoming. RuntimeConfig: tick_period 2ms, egress_period 1ms, append_notify_timeout 1500ms; case 1/2 use event_capacity 64, case 3 uses 8. ServerConfig: election_tick_timeout 3, resend_message_tick_timeout 5, batch_size 1. Case 3 subscribes and drains events only on pid 1; pids 2 and 3 leave the receiver the handle owns unread, so after enough observed transitions their event channels fill and their actors park. It keeps paced ordinary writes coming from the elected leader, waits until two of the three nodes stop answering commands, then requires: node 1 still answers; node 1's `append_notify_with_timeout(_, 300ms)` resolves with Timeout (its own actor runs, so that endpoint is reachable) rather than Ok; node 1's decided index is unchanged one second later. It emits CA_EVENT parked_majority_cluster {nodes_parked,healthy_node_responsive,append_notify_timeout_reached,decided_before,decided_after}.

revision_reason: Adds a third case to the same harness (existing two cases and their assertions unchanged except that case 1 now waits for at least one parked node and asserts the full-and-live channel on the parked nodes, plus 25s windows and 6x paced proposals so it is not sensitive to how many nodes reach the bound first). New case `parked_majority_stops_the_cluster_deciding`: a 3-node cluster where only node 1 drains its event stream (event_capacity 8), nodes 2 and 3 park, and the healthy node 1 must then be unable to complete a write - it reports the documented Timeout for an append_notify with a 300ms deadline, and its decided index is unchanged across the attempt.
